overview: Narrative review of approaches to tracking follow-up of incidental imaging findings, organised by the points where the loop breaks, with completion reported alongside each study's design, setting and definitions, for the radiology quality committee on 14 January 2027.
population: Adults with an incidental imaging finding that carries a follow-up recommendation (lung, adrenal, renal, thyroid, pancreatic and liver findings); reports from any health system, in English or French, published 2010 to 2026.
exposure: Tracking approaches: structured recommendation codes, tracking lists, navigators, automated clinician alerts, letters or portal messages to patients, and combinations of these.
procedures: The librarian searches three bibliographic databases and the grey literature of radiology and patient safety bodies, and the reviewers follow citations of included reports. Two radiologists screen and extract together, recording approach, setting, finding types, the completion definition (window and denominator), failure points, resources, and results for patients without a primary care clinician, emergency-only patients and patients who need an interpreter. Every figure cited to the committee is checked against its source record first; unverified leads, including the national benchmark lead, are listed separately and not cited.

outcomes.name: Follow-up completion within the recommended interval
outcomes.measure: Proportion of recommendations with completed follow-up imaging within the interval each study states, recorded with its window and denominator
outcomes.why: The outcome every approach claims to improve and the one the spot check measured.

outcomes.name: Later-stage diagnoses after missed follow-up
outcomes.measure: Cancers or other serious diagnoses made at a later stage in flagged lesions, as reported
outcomes.why: The harm the department is trying to prevent.

outcomes.name: Acknowledgement by a responsible clinician
outcomes.measure: Proportion of recommendations acknowledged by a clinician, as reported

outcomes.name: Patient worry and unnecessary imaging
outcomes.measure: Reported worry after direct communication and follow-up imaging judged unnecessary
outcomes.why: Direct letters and aggressive tracking can harm as well as help.

feasibility: Three months: month 1 search and screening, month 2 extraction, month 3 synthesis and committee report; three librarian days and two radiologists' time, as approved.
biasMitigation: Completion definitions recorded with every figure; no pooling
Every figure cited to the committee checked against its source record
Unverified leads kept in a separate list and never cited as evidence

biasFlags.label: Publication of successes
biasFlags.note: Programmes that failed are less often published; grey literature is searched.

biasFlags.label: Incomparable completion definitions
biasFlags.note: Handled by reporting definitions rather than pooling.

biasFlags.label: Single academic centres
biasFlags.note: Settings may not match a department without navigators or a tracking list.

flags: One primary outcome with its definition; one process and one balancing measure
parsimony.simplestPath: One review question, one extraction form, one table per approach organised by failure point.

theoreticalFramework: A closed-loop communication model (recommendation, receipt, acknowledgement, action, completion) organises the failure points; no other framework.
summary: Three-month narrative review; one primary outcome with its definition, one secondary, one process and one balancing measure.
